label: u (or w) as the 4th original token (also weakly u as the 1st)
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, never at <DEL> or in the copy phase, and only at steps t=0,2,3,4 (never t=1 or t>=5). About 78% of activation mass is at t=3. The input token matters most: u (15.6x lift), then w, then b, with 0/v weaker. The largest activations (up to max) are u or w at t=3 when the previous token is r, e.g. p r r [u]. Other previous tokens (g, f, l, y) also raise it. At t=0 it fires weakly on u, which makes up many activations but little mass. Smaller activations at t=2 and t=4 follow the same token preferences. Almost all activations are first occurrences of the token. The tendency is graded, an additive mix of position, current token and previous token, so a token/position rule only partly captures it. Activations not covered: b/0/v/other tokens at t=3 after r, and t=2/t=4 cases. False positives: u/w at t=3 without a favorable previous token often stay below threshold.
